title: Lessons from building GenAI based applications — Juan Peredo
talk_summary: A practitioner's survey of GenAI application lessons: model hosting choices, guardrails/RAG/fine-tuning tradeoffs, evaluation tooling, externalized prompts, agent latency/cost math, and observability.

takeaways.what_they_do: Use OpenRouter-style routing that, for a given model, picks the cheapest provider offering it, and deliberately substitute a smaller/cheaper model when the task allows.
takeaways.evidence_quote: they will run it until the one that's against the one that's cheaper which is really cool and it's a great way to save money
takeaways.numbers: O1 example: $24/call, $9,270/day, ~$300k/month; swapping to Llama 3.3 70B drops to $0.52/call and ~$50k/month (~6x cheaper)

takeaways.what_they_do: Keep prompts in a shared hub/repo so non-coders can edit and test them, and so a model swap only requires prompt retuning rather than code changes.
takeaways.evidence_quote: promp should never be encoded in your code

takeaways.what_they_do: Record per-step traces (each LLM/tool call, inputs, outputs, errors, metadata) so non-deterministic multi-node agent failures can be diagnosed.
takeaways.evidence_quote: things that were running a 100 times with no issue will start failing out 100 1001st item

takeaways.what_they_do: Use eval tooling (LangSmith-like) to record runs and compare model/prompt performance over time at each dev stage.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it lets you constantly evaluate your models so it will uh it can help you record uh a number of Bruns

takeaways.what_they_do: Use framework branching/concurrency so independent sub-calls run in parallel instead of serially, cutting wall-clock latency.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if each one of these things took um two seconds instead of these things taking eight seconds all of a sudden it takes six
takeaways.numbers: 8s serial vs ~6s parallel in their example

takeaways.technique: Guardrail as cheap classifier, not big model
takeaways.what_they_do: Put a small secondary LLM as a classifier in front of the main model to filter/route, accepting added latency and cost.
takeaways.evidence_quote: adding this secondary LM adds latency because you're making a secondary call right and it also has additional cost
